mainTopic: End of the proof about indirect damage from the broken vineyard fence (כלאי הכרם), and a new משנה about a dyer who ruins or wrongly dyes wool
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא about a vineyard owner whose fence broke. He was warned again and again but gave up and did not repair it. He is held liable for the neighbor's grain that became forbidden as כלאי הכרם, even though he did nothing active. The גמרא uses this to show that רבי מאיר holds a person liable for indirect damage. Then a new משנה begins about a dyer. If he burned the wool in the pot, he pays the wool's value. If he dyed it badly (כָּאוּר), the owner pays him only the smaller amount: his expenses or the value he added. If he used the wrong color, רבי מאיר says he pays for the wool, and רבי יהודה says he is paid the smaller amount. The גמרא starts to explain the word כָּאוּר as כַּלְבּוֹס, and רבה בר שמואל's explanation of that word comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The neglected vineyard fence makes the owner liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: if the vineyard owner gives up on his broken fence and doesn't repair it, he has made the neighbor's grain forbidden and must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The grain owner tells him, "Fence it!" If it broke again, he tells him again, "Fence it!" If the vineyard owner gave up on it and did not fence it, he has made the grain forbidden, and he must pay for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא it brought as proof. A vineyard owner who ignores repeated warnings to fix his fence must pay for the grain that becomes forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vineyard owner did no active deed. He only failed to fix the fence, and the vines then made the grain forbidden as כלאי הכרם. Even so, he is חייב. The גמרא uses this to show that רבי מאיר makes a person pay for damage he caused indirectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Responsibility to pay for the loss

steps.whatToRemember: Even someone who caused a loss just by neglect, after being warned, can be liable to pay.

phrases.english: He tells him, "Fence it!"
phrases.notes: The grain owner is telling the vineyard owner to fix the broken fence between the vines and the grain.

phrases.english: If it broke open again, he tells him, "Fence it!"
If he gave up on it and did not fence it,
he has made the grain forbidden,
and he is responsible to pay for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִתְיָיאֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה וְלֹא גְּדָרָהּ הֲרֵי זֶה קִידֵּשׁ וְחַיָּיב בְּאַחְרָיוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא the גמרא began quoting just before this section, as proof about רבי מאיר's view on indirect damage.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds a person liable for indirect damage (דינא דגרמי)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the vineyard owner who neglects his broken fence and is held חייב באחריותו

steps.title: A dyer who burns the wool or dyes it badly
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules: if the dyer burned the wool, he pays its value. If he dyed it badly, the owner pays him only the smaller of his expenses or the added value.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone gives wool to a dyer and it got burned in the pot, the dyer pays him the value of his wool. If he dyed it badly: if the improvement is more than the expenses, the owner pays him the expenses. If the expenses are more than the improvement, the owner pays him the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about a dyer who did a bad job. It gives two cases: wool that was totally ruined, and wool that was dyed poorly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the wool is burned, nothing was gained, so the dyer simply pays for the wool he ruined. When the dye job is poor but still adds some value, the dyer is paid the lower of two amounts: his costs or the value he added. A dyer who did a bad job never comes out ahead.
steps.confusionAlert: In the כָּאוּר case, the one who pays is the wool owner, paying the dyer. The dyer is the one who pays only in the burned case.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who gives wool to a dyer,
and the pot burned it,
the dyer gives him the value of his wool.
If he dyed it badly,
if the improvement is more than the expenses,
the owner gives him the expenses;
phrases.notes: From here on, the wool owner is paying the dyer, not the other way around.

phrases.english: and if the expenses are more than the improvement,
he gives him the improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dyer who burned the wool pays its value. A dyer who dyed it badly receives the lesser of his expenses or the improvement.

steps.title: Dyed the wrong color: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree
steps.stepSummary: If the dyer used the wrong color, רבי מאיר says he pays the value of the wool. רבי יהודה says he gets the lesser of his expenses or the improvement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the owner told him to dye it red and he dyed it black, or black and he dyed it red: רבי מאיר says the dyer gives him the value of his wool. רבי יהודה says: if the improvement is more than the expenses, the owner gives him the expenses. If the expenses are more than the improvement, he gives him the improvement.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a third case, where the dyer used a different color than he was asked to. Two תנאים argue about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats the wrong color like the burned case: the dyer pays for the wool. רבי יהודה treats it like the כָּאוּר case: the owner keeps the dyed wool and pays the dyer only the lower of his expenses or the improvement. The משנה gives the ruling only, without reasons.
steps.whatToRemember: Burned wool means the dyer pays the wool's value. Badly dyed wool means the dyer gets the smaller of expenses or improvement. Wrong color is a מחלוקת between these two models: רבי מאיר follows the first and רבי יהודה follows the second.

phrases.english: If he gave it to dye red for him and he dyed it black,
or black and he dyed it red,
Rabbi Meir says:
The dyer gives him the value of his wool.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If the improvement is more than the expenses,
the owner gives him the expenses,
and if the expenses are more than the improvement,
he gives him the improvement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third case to the משנה, where the two rulings of step 2 become a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wrong color: רבי מאיר says the dyer pays the wool's value. רבי יהודה says the dyer receives the lesser of his expenses or the improvement.

steps.title: What does כָּאוּר mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה's word כָּאוּר means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the meaning of an unclear word in the משנה. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling about expenses and improvement depends on what kind of bad dye job the משנה means. Before analyzing the law, the גמרא first pins down the word.

keyTerms.meaning: What is, what does it mean

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is "ka'ur"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word from the second case of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כָּאוּר in the משנה

steps.title: כָּאוּר means כַּלְבּוֹס
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר בר חנה, says כָּאוּר means כַּלְבּוֹס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said that רבה בר בר חנה said: It means כַּלְבּוֹס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another word, כַּלְבּוֹס. That word is also unclear, which leads to the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a description, the answer gives a different term that people then used. That term also needs explaining, so the גמרא keeps going.

keyTerms.meaning: A term for a kind of bad dyeing, explained next

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar bar Chana said:
"Kelabus."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה כַּלְבּוֹס

steps.title: What does כַּלְבּוֹס mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כַּלְבּוֹס means and introduces רבה בר שמואל's answer, which comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is כַּלְבּוֹס? רבה בר שמואל said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word it was just given. It starts to introduce רבה בר שמואל's explanation, which comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second layer of word clarification. The answer itself comes on the next amud; only the name of the one answering appears here.

phrases.english: What is "kelabus"?
Rabba bar Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: His actual explanation comes at the top of the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the term given as the answer in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word כַּלְבּוֹס
